reviews.title: Horribly inaccurate
reviews.text:
I’ve been using this for about 4 weeks now. I had heard that the app isn’t the most accurate, but that the margin of error was pretty immaterial. I have found the margin of error significant. Especially for the last few days. Yesterday I took a photo of my lunch which included 6 cherry tomatoes, which were easily separately identifiable. The app estimated that there were 800g of tomatoes on my plate! It also read my quartered scotch egg as 3 scotch eggs. Of course, the calorie estimate was over 3 x the actual meal. I’m constantly having to go in and edit the ingredients and quantities. Attempting to use the fix issue button seems to confuse things further and I end up having to delete the entry and start again. Today, it has changed the micro nutrients in my saved cup of tea, and now thinks there are 44mg of sodium in one cup - it’s black tea with milk!

What swung this app for me was the interaction with the Apple Health app, but that doesn’t work all that well. The calorie burn I see on my move ring in fitness is always higher than what appears in Cal AI. And every time a workout is loaded, an error message comes up about duplicated calories.

The app does not do everything it promises, and I would not buy it again.

reviews.title: So inaccurate!
reviews.text: I have the paid version and no matter how many times you update the app, it just makes so many mistakes. It’s ridiculous. I’m just warning everyone, it keeps getting the numbers wrong. I even reached out to support one time and they acknowledged that the app has its limitations. For example, I’ll scan a barcode and the number the app records is 30 calories more than what the product with the barcode says. That type of stuff shouldn’t be happening. Another example, the app will make a mistake like that and then I’ll use the “fix it” option and I’ll say something like “it’s not 280 calories, it’s 250” and then it will update it but let’s say that the protein count was correct and it was 10 grams, all of a sudden it will be 7 grams! So then you have to tell the AI, no, it’s 250 calories and 10 grams of protein, and then it will still do it wrong three times and then you just give up. This app is maddening.

reviews.title: Everything it does myfitnesspal does better
reviews.text:
Cal AI really struggles with identifying portion sizes, which is what I hoped it would be better at doing than MFP.  It struggles to count clearly visible food items, like cherry tomatoes.  It will routinely get the number of things wrong. It also can’t read the nutrition information on a label that you scan, so you have to manually change everything anyway. Why did I pay money when myfitnesspal does this better, FOR FREE?  
It also gives you incredibly unhelpful advice in its assessment of your daily diet. For example, I do an intense exercise and log it, and cal ai recommends a number of calories I should eat to sustain myself with this additional expenditure of energy. I will eat maybe 75% of the recommended calories that the new total recommended because I’m just not hungry and I’m trying to satiety.  The app is supposed to roll over some of your calories to the next day if you have leftover. Cal ai will sometimes flip out and insist I overate.  
It also applauds me on the days where I eat under 1000 calories (the recommended rate I should be eating is 1250/day).  

So if I can’t rely on 
- the calories in food being accurate
- getting accurate feedback on calories being burned through movement 
- any of the health advice it’s spitting out 

Why am I paying for this?

reviews.title: Poor Customer Support and Unclear Marketing - THINK TWICE
reviews.text:
I bought the individual plan first, then purchased the Family Plan believing it would upgrade or replace my existing subscription. That is not what happened.

After purchasing the Family Plan, I learned through Cal AI support that both subscriptions remain active separately. Because the individual plan was purchased first, the Family Plan could not actually be used as intended until the individual plan term ended. By that point, most of the Family Plan subscription period would already be gone.

I contacted support multiple times. For weeks, I was told the issue had been escalated to billing. Later, support clarified that because the purchase was through Apple, they could not process the refund and Apple was the only refund path. Apple denied the refund request and appeal, so I paid for a Family Plan that was effectively unusable for the reason I bought it.

The app may work for some people, but my experience with the subscription structure and support process was extremely frustrating. If you are upgrading from an individual plan to a family plan, be very careful before purchasing. Make sure you understand exactly when the Family Plan will become usable, because it may not replace your individual plan the way you expect.

reviews.title: Fraudulent Charges and Terrible Customer Service
reviews.text:
I wanted to love this app, but the first red flag was when I was charged immediately on the third day of use after being told I would be notified before my three day free trial was up. Second red flag was when my premium features stopped working after a week of use. Their customer service was absolutely useless - they respond quickly but make you explain the situation multiple times to get to a reasonsble explanation. They eventually escalated my issue to the technical team, which yielded no response. It got so frustrating that I asked for a refund and to cancel my subscription. I was told that it was escalated to their internal billing team then days ago by without any update so I followed up just to be told that I need to request a refund through Apple. The charge on my bank statement was clearly made by their company and not Apple subscriptions. There is also no evidence in my Apple account that a subscription 
with this company was initiated through Apple (and I’ve done this many times before through Apple with other apps). The lack of accountability was jarring. The right people are not talking to each other internally, and their operations are clearly faulty. I’ll be filing a fraudulent dispute with my bank and hoping I never have to deal with this company again.

reviews.title: More bugs than features
reviews.text: I’ll start with the positives; the layout is nice and clean (compared to MyFitnessPal which is a disaster of too much stuff), their customer service/support team is super responsive so you know they are getting your feedback. However, I only know this because I’ve had to email them a dozen times. The idea is great but terribly flawed. It’s another attempt at full reliance on “AI” with zero checks and balances. When scanning a food by label or barcode, it gets the macros and calories correct about 50% of the time - sometimes it doesn’t even get the food right. That does not give me a lot of confidence on how often it’s gonna be right from a photo of a meal. It’s got a very weird way of counting and displaying total and average calories and expenditure and does not count for BMR in the calorie burn. There’s no way to see if you are running a caloric surplus or deficit or to see your average macros over a given period.  You can copy a previously eaten food to another date, except for today’s date. Someone on their programming team willfully and purposefully excluded the one and only day you would ever want to copy something to. It also does not write data to Apple health (or anywhere else for that matter) so if you want to see your fitness and nutrition in one spot, this isn’t the place.  Had super high hopes for this but there’s just so many things that need to be corrected. Their ads say some kid built it because spending all the time tracking macros didn’t fit into his life -

reviews.title: Dangerous goals + deceptive billing
reviews.text:
This app suggested an intake of 980 calories for me (150 lb female, trying to gradually lose 15 lb in a few months). For comparison, other apps suggested 1600 calories as a good target for my goals. This app actually had a slider to adjust how quickly you want to lose weight that allowed it to drop down to <400 calories a day. 
In addition to setting dangerous, unhealthy caloric targets, their billing is also deceptive. They charge you with Apple Pay, not a subscription in the App Store. So to cancel, you can’t manage the subscription the way you do for other apps. There is no option to view or manage billing within the app settings. You have to go to their website online and enter your email - and that also didn’t work, so I’m having to contact support. I did the 3 day trial and am trying to cancel it before I am charged, and they make you jump through way too many hoops. It is shocking that this app has so many positive reviews unless they are fake and paid.

reviews.title: Be Warned - Dangerous Advice
reviews.text: UI is good and the AI Detection works moderately well (though is often wrong, for example, I took a picture of 8 grapes this morning and it told me that was 8 servies of grapes and was over 700 calories). My biggest issue with this app is the calorie advice. I said that I was 33 years old, female, 145 lbs, and that I work out 2X a week. I wanted to lose 10 lbs in 2 months (which is an understandably aggressive goal) but it told me to eat a max of 682 calories a day. I personally feel that's a dangerous and inaccurate target, especially for a moderately active person. I do see that if you log exercises it will add to that number, but if you're not constntly logging your steps/exercise/ daily calorie ependiture (which occurs outside of just exercising), you're going to be seriously underconsuming. As with any health recommendations, definitely prioritize real doctors and sources over AI, but I put this same information in other AI Sources (Chat GPT/Gemini/etc) and all sources said that 682 was a dangerous calorie limit that could lead to hormone disruption/muscle loss/etc. So if you want to use this app for calorie tracking, by all means. But please please cross check any health advice coming from this app across other sources.

reviews.title: AI hallucinating?
reviews.text:
I like the interface and idea of this app a lot - but feel I can’t trust it. For example, I took a photo of nachos last night, and it accurately identified basically all of the ingredients - impressive! But then when I click into each ingredient, it has macros that make no sense - like 9g of protein for 1 cup of tortilla chips. I wish lol! (For reference, unless protein is added, tortilla chips are typically 1g protein/cup). Things like this happen a lot. I also often scan the nutrition label of food, and then enter the exact g amount that I consume, and when I adjust the g in the app to specify how much I ate it is unable to do that conversion and just keeps the food as 1 serving… even though that is fairly simple math. Finally, the food database is pretty limited and it seems to not be learning - like if I scan a nutrition label and add the label and brand of that food, it doesn’t show up in the library, and I instead have to pull from my saved foods, but that means the app is missing out on so much knowledge it could be crowdsourcing. 

I hope these issues are fixed, because then I would love the app. Also, the 3 day trial feels really short, I only recognized these issues after a week of consistent use, so that feels icky to now be paying for a year.

reviews.title: Deceptive App
reviews.text: This app is basically a textbook example of what not to do. I mean it. I’m literally going to roast it in front of my university UI/UX students. It makes good promises, gathers all your data, then hits you with a paywall with no free version available (not even a very limited one). BUT even the sign up screen is deceptive, meant to trick people into paying for a year (I’m sure they know people give up within a few months). The monthly price is 3× as high as the per-month price if you buy a year’s worth. If users are going to give you all their data they should have the transparency up front that you’re going to corner them into bad subscription options. At the VERY least you should give them an option to delete all the data they just gave you when they bail. By the way, they offer 80% off if you try to navigate away from the sale screen. This app seemed so promising. The ideas are awesome and the UI looks intuitive. It’s a shame they completely torch their users’ trust before they even get started.

reviews.title: Do not fall for this.
reviews.text: I don’t know why on earth there are so many good reviews. As someone who has been heavy lifting for 4 years, and who spent almost a decade recovering from an eating disorder and healing my relationship with food, this app is a trap and subtly encourages eating disorders. Every meal I ever inputted first of all was usually incorrect, second, ALWAYS labeled 3/10 on the stupid health score that is in NO WAY ACCURATE. It tried to tell me that GREEK YOGURT is unhealthier in a homemade chicken salad than MULTIPLE SERVINGS OF MAYO. It does not actually know what a “healthy meal is” and critiques everything you eat. It had me confused for a minute when I let my mind get in the way of all the work I’ve done to recover. I have defined abs and more muscle on my body than most average gym goers and this thing is trying to tell me what I’m eating is unhealthy… I eat all Whole Foods, no processed junk snacks, just real raw ingredients. Do not give this app your money like I did. Find another app. And to anyone who has lost significant weight because of this app- that’s not a good thing. I guarantee you that. You can be UNHEALTHY and skinny. And this app is getting you on the road for that.

I  feel I owe it to others so they don't feel the same over the course of their subscription. 
If you are using this type of app, I'm guessing you are on a mission and this  was part of it.  Logging and tracking is important and you are in a committed pattern then all of a sudden you are dead in the water.  
I can't even get my money back because no one ever actually helps you with figuring out how to get back into your account!

reviews.title: Ok for basics, but custom meals and recipes lack features common in other apps.
reviews.text: Purchased this app to track my calories and water intake, however after discussing with other people and seeing what they use to track I see that this app is falling behind and it’s custom meals and portioning. There needs to be a way to add an entire recipe with all the ingredients, list how many portions it makes, then you can say how many portions you ate of that entire recipe which is not possible here. Another major drawback is I paid $30 for the appand because I forgot to fill out my tracker Christmas day I now have to pay a dollar to get my streak back which is unacceptable. I could see charging non-premium members, but to take my money for something so little and then still have to charge me additional if I miss a day every so often is ridiculous. I canceled my subscription on this alone and I’m debating returning the app and requesting a refund… like every month you should get some free passes and that would fix everything.

reviews.title: Doesn't feel like a serious health tracking tool
reviews.text:
If you want a serious adult health app, this isn't it. If you prefer a noisy, badge collecting, pop up heavy game that happens to involve some food tracking you might enjoy it.

Constant pop ups and pointless badges, streaks and meaningless achievements completely ruin the experience. Every action seems to trigger another notification, celebration or badge, which gets irritating very quickly. If you are genuinely trying to track health, this level of gamification is more distracting and time consuming than motivating or functional. 

The core functionality is buried under a child like gaming experience 

It’s noisy, annoying, and feels designed to maximise taps rather than help users make informed health decisions.

reviews.title: Locked behind a paywall
reviews.text:
In order to get any sort of access to this app, you’re forced to set up a subscription. And they only tell you this after first making you create an account and input all your personal details. 
Some may say it’s ‘marketing’ but it just seems like cheap, dishonest behaviour - making people waste time installing and setting it all up only to have no access to the app whatsoever until beginning a subscription. The 4-5 star rating is misleading and only exists because they urge you to leave a positive review 2 minutes into using the app.

reviews.title: Stuck in a 38-Message Support Loop and Still No Solution
reviews.text:
I normally never leave negative reviews, but my experience with Cal AI’s support has been unbelievably frustrating.

I upgraded to the Family Plan, was charged instantly, and the app never unlocked the feature. The Family Plan page only showed “Upgrade to Family Plan,” even though I had already paid.

I reached out to support, and what followed was a 38-message loop of repeated, copy-and-paste responses. I provided multiple screenshots, videos, and detailed explanations. Their replies ignored everything I sent and simply asked me to do the exact same steps over and over, steps that clearly did not solve the problem.
￼
Every time I explained that the issue persisted, they asked for “another screenshot” of the same page I had already sent multiple times. It became very obvious that nobody was actually reading the conversation.

After days of this, I still have:

• No access to the Family Plan
• No fix for the account conflict
• No straightforward path to a refund
• No meaningful help from support

I genuinely liked the app before this, but this experience has shown me that if anything goes wrong, there is no real support system behind it.

Until Cal AI fixes their subscription management and massively improves their customer support, I cannot recommend this app to anyone, especially not if you’re considering paying for a premium plan.

reviews.title: Has potential but poor
reviews.text: Easy to use but has small database of food. Too many every day English foods are not recognised and when you scan the image it will not portion the meal. Also when the app does recognise the food the calorie data is often hugely incorrect.. I mean way off. Final gripe… I accepted this app on a monthly basis and when I paid it charged me for the whole year… if the app was accurate I would have been happy.. but it’s not so I’m not. Stick to MyFitnessPal.. it’s more accurate and doesn’t try and stitch you up.
